title: Swiss Glaciers Lose More Ice in 2026
paragraphs: A new report says that Swiss glaciers lost more than 5 percent of their ice in 2026. Scientists measure the glaciers every year. The report was published on 1 October.

The winter of 2025 and 2026 was one of the ten winters with the least snow since measurements began. Then the summer was very warm. On 76 days, the freezing point was higher than 4,000 metres, which is more than twice the usual number.

Two small glaciers, Bella Tola and Griessfirn, disappeared completely. In five years, Switzerland has lost nearly 20 percent of its glacier ice. The glaciers also sent a lot of water into rivers in the summer.
